rules.title: Method call on a trait-object receiver dispatches via vtable
rules.statement: A method call `recv.m(..)` where `recv: dyn Trait` (or `&dyn Trait`/`&mut dyn Trait`, i.e. a reference whose pointee is a trait object) and the method has a vtable slot is dispatched dynamically through the receiver's vtable at that slot; references to a trait object load the dyn handle once before dispatch.

rules.title: Primitive/value receiver is auto-referenced for &self
rules.statement: When the method's `self` is `&self`/`&mut self` but the receiver is a by-value primitive (i8/i16/i32/i64, u8/u16/u32/u64, f32/f64, bool, char), the receiver value is materialized into storage and a pointer to it is passed as the self argument.

rules.title: Receiver passed as method's first argument
rules.statement: A method call lowers to a call whose argument 0 is the receiver (self) and arguments 1..n are the call's explicit arguments; explicit argument i maps to callee parameter i+1.

rules.title: Method argument concrete→trait-object unsize coercion
rules.statement: When a method parameter has type `dyn Trait` (a trait object, possibly after peeling one `Box<_>` layer) and the supplied argument is a non-trait-object concrete type, the argument is unsize-coerced into a fat `{data, vtable}` handle for that trait built from the argument's concrete type; this coercion applies symmetrically to free-function and method calls.

rules.title: Aggregate / tagged-enum argument passed by pointer
rules.statement: An argument whose value is an aggregate (struct) or a tagged (data-carrying) enum, passed where the callee parameter is pointer-represented, is materialized into storage and passed by pointer; scalar arguments are numerically coerced to the parameter type instead.

rules.title: Fat-reference struct fields are stored inline; read yields the slot address
rules.statement: A struct field of slice, closure, custom-DST-reference, fat-zone-mut, or relative-offset representation is stored inline within the struct (a 16-byte fat pair for the always-fat subset), and a field read yields the address of that inline storage (materializing a relative offset to an absolute pointer where applicable), not a by-value load. A tuple-typed field likewise yields its inline slot address. A trait-object field is excluded and read by value.

rules.title: Scalar struct field read loads the value
rules.statement: A struct field whose type is not an inline-fat/aggregate kind is read by loading the value at the field's address.

rules.title: Unsigned index operand zero-extends to 64-bit
rules.statement: When indexing with an unsigned integer index (u8/u16/u24/u32/u56/u64/u128) narrower than 64 bits, the index is zero-extended to 64 bits before address computation.

rules.title: Aggregate array/buffer elements stored inline; indexing yields slot address
rules.statement: Elements of arrays and contiguous buffers whose element type is a struct, a tagged enum, a closure, a slice, a trait object, or a tuple are stored inline (sizeof(elem) per slot); an index read strides by the inline footprint and yields the address of the element slot (the value of such kinds being represented by a pointer to its storage), not a by-value load of a pointer-width prefix. Scalar elements are loaded by value.

rules.title: Indexing through a reference/pointer to an array strides by element
rules.statement: Indexing a value of type `&[T;N]`, `&mut [T;N]`, or `*[T;N]` uses the SSA pointer directly as the address of element 0 and strides by the element type; the array is not loaded by value.

rules.title: Indexing a *dyn Trait pointer loads an 8-byte dyn handle per slot
rules.statement: Indexing a `*const/*mut dyn Trait` (pointer whose pointee is a trait object) strides by pointer width per slot and loads the dyn handle; `p[0]` is the index form of `*p`.

rules.title: Tuple elements stored inline by value
rules.statement: A tuple stores each element inline by value at its layout slot; constructing a tuple writes each element into its slot, copying inline-aggregate (struct/array) elements by value rather than storing a pointer, and a tuple value is represented as a pointer to its storage.

rules.title: Tuple-index auto-derefs a reference receiver
rules.statement: A tuple index `t.k` where `t: &(..)`/`&mut(..)`/`*(..)` (reference/pointer whose pointee is a tuple) operates on the pointee tuple; the receiver pointer is used directly as the tuple address.

rules.title: Tuple-index of inline-aggregate element yields its address
rules.statement: A tuple index `t.k` whose element type is a struct, tagged enum, slice, closure, trait object, or nested tuple yields the address of the inline element slot (the value being pointer-represented); scalar elements are loaded by value. A by-value tuple result is first materialized into storage before address computation.
